column1: # OWASP ZAP baseline scan rules for the DAST job (.github/workflows/dast.yml).
# Tab-separated: <alertId>
#   action = IGNORE  — accepted / not applicable, never fails the scan
#            WARN     — reported, does not fail the scan (default for anything not listed)
#            FAIL     — reported and fails the scan
#   url-regex — omit (empty 3rd column) to apply to every URL; otherwise a Python
#               regex matched against the finding's URL
# Posture: BLOCKING (fail-action: true in dast.yml) — every finding below has been
# judged and accepted; a NEW un-IGNOREd WARN/FAIL now fails the scan.
# alert IDs: https://www.zaproxy.org/docs/alerts/
# --- Triaged from the 2026-09-11 unauthenticated baseline of the full Aspire stack
#     (Keycloak + MockBusinessApp + TestSite), after SEC-PT2-004's two real header/cookie
#     regressions were root-caused and fixed (#193 OnStarting header-survival, #194
#     antiforgery X-Frame-Options duplication, #195 antiforgery cookie Secure flag). ---
# --- 2026-09-12 (#203): CSP promoted from Report-Only to enforced (SEC-PT2-004's own
#     "tune then enforce" plan, now complete) — the "CSP Header Not Set" [10038] IGNORE
#     entry that used to live here is gone: it was excusing a real, deliberately-open gap
#     (ZAP only recognises the enforced header), not a false positive, so removing the
#     excuse rather than updating its wording is correct now that the header is genuinely
#     present. Enforcing surfaced one new real finding, fixed properly, not IGNOREd:
#     "Failure to Define Directive with No Fallback" [10055] — object-src and base-uri
#     don't fall back to default-src per spec, so PrismSecurityHeadersOptions' default
#     policy now sets both explicitly (object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'). ---
# ---- /umbraco* : the Umbraco backoffice owns its own header + CSP regime ----
# PrismSecurityHeadersMiddleware is deliberately scoped to skip /umbraco* by default
# (PrismSecurityHeadersOptions.ExcludeBackoffice — a Lit web-component SPA a strict CSP
# would break), the same posture Wayfinder.Umbraco's own reference-app middleware ships.
# A real deployment fronts the backoffice with its own policy (reverse proxy / WAF), and
# it is often not publicly reachable at all. Each line is path-scoped so the identical
# header regressing on the *front end* still fails the scan.

column4: X-Content-Type-Options: backoffice + its static assets, Umbraco-owned
HSTS: backoffice + its static assets, Umbraco-owned
informational: the backoffice is a SPA

column1: # Re-examine Cache-control Directives — the app explicitly sends
# "Cache-control: no-cache, no-store" + "Pragma: no-cache" on every dynamic page (an
# anti-caching stance, stricter than default, not weaker); ZAP's heuristic flags the
# directive combination for review regardless of which way it errs. Correct behaviour.

column4: explicit no-cache/no-store on dynamic pages — a stricter, not weaker, stance

column1: # Storable and Cacheable Content — informational cache-control notes on immutable static
# assets (CSS), robots.txt, sitemap.xml (both legitimately 404 — this app has neither),
# and the anonymous landing page. Correct behaviour.

column4: informational cache-control notes on static assets + the anonymous landing page

column1: # Cookie with SameSite Attribute None — the OIDC nonce + correlation cookies
# (.AspNetCore.OpenIdConnect.Nonce.*, .AspNetCore.Correlation.*) on /auth/login and
# /auth/register, minted by Microsoft.Identity.Web ahead of the redirect to Keycloak.
# SameSite=None is required for the cross-origin OIDC redirect round-trip to survive;
# verified live (curl -I) both cookies also carry Secure + HttpOnly, so this is the
# correct, necessary configuration for the flow, not a gap.

column4: OIDC nonce/correlation cookies — SameSite=None required for the redirect round-trip, Secure+HttpOnly confirmed

column1: # Suspicious Comments — plain English prose comments (verified: no secrets, no
# security-relevant TODO markers) in both the shared Wayfinder rendering JS and
# TestSite's own authored front-end JS.

column4: prose words in genuine code comments

column1: # Timestamp Disclosure (Unix) in vendored GOV.UK Frontend CSS — a numeric literal in the
# minified stylesheet, not a timestamp. Third-party vendored asset.

column4: numeric literal in minified vendored CSS

column1: # Session Management Response Identified — informational; ZAP spotting the ASP.NET
# antiforgery / TempData / PrismPublicServiceRequestVisitor cookies on the service-request
# journey POSTs and the caseworker worklist. Expected.

column4: informational: ASP.NET antiforgery / TempData / visitor-correlation cookies

column1: # Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy Header Missing or Invalid — COEP: require-corp exists only
# to enable cross-origin isolation (SharedArrayBuffer, high-resolution timers), which this
# app does not use. PrismSecurityHeadersMiddleware does not set COOP or CORP either, by
# the same reasoning — there is no cross-origin-isolation use case anywhere in Prism.

column4: COEP (and COOP/CORP) only matter for cross-origin isolation, which this app does not use
